title: Meta Analysis of Diagnostic Test Evaluation
author: Chuandan Wan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8t4hwqw
materials: studies published in languages other than English.

steps.title: Perform Literature Search
steps.instruction: Systematically search PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and WANFANG medicine online databases for relevant articles without language or regional limitations, ending the search on March 18, 2019.

substeps.instruction: Use search terms: “cervical cancer AND ctDNA”, “cervix cancer AND ctDNA”, “cervical carcinoma AND ctDNA” OR “circulating DNA AND cervical cancer”, including various alterations in spelling and abbreviations.
Screen titles and abstracts for relevance.
Remove duplicate entries.
Retrieve full text of reports meeting preliminary criteria.

steps.title: Select Eligible Studies
steps.instruction: Assess retrieved articles based on specific inclusion and exclusion criteria.

substeps.instruction: Apply inclusion criteria: (1) evaluated diagnostic accuracy of quantitative ctDNA analysis in cervical cancer; (2) diagnostic value reported or calculable from data; (3) full text and all data available; (4) techniques and target genes clearly stated; (5) at least 10 patients with cervical cancer and relevant negative controls.

Apply exclusion criteria: (1) diagnostic/prognostic value cannot be deduced from incomplete data; (2) repeated studies from the same group; (3) sample size < 10; (4) data only from cell line experiments; (5) published in languages other than English.
If the same patient population is used in several studies, include only the most recent one.

steps.title: Review and Extract Data
steps.instruction: Perform independent review and data extraction of eligible studies.

substeps.instruction: Have two reviewers (CD Wan and YL Gu) independently evaluate studies using the Newcastle-Ottawa scale, settling disagreements via a third researcher and discussion.
Extract basic feature data: authors’ names, country, sample type, detection method, numbers of experimental and control groups, and analysis indicators.
Extract outcome indicators: positives, false positives, false negatives, true negatives, sensitivity, and specificity.
Evaluate methodological quality and risk of bias using QUADAS-2 Guidelines.

steps.title: Perform Statistical Meta-Analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the extracted data using Meta-DiSc 1.4 and STATA 14.0 software following standard methods for diagnostic test evaluations.

substeps.instruction: Calculate sensitivity (proportion of ctDNA presence in confirmed cervical cancer patients) and specificity (proportion of negative ctDNA detection in negative control volunteers).
Calculate Positive Likelihood Ratio (PLR) as sensitivity/(1 – specificity).
Calculate Negative Likelihood Ratio (NLR) as (1 – sensitivity)/specificity.
Calculate Diagnostic Odds Ratio (DOR) as PLR / NLR.
Summarize indicators using a bivariate meta-analysis model.
Determine threshold effect using ROC curve and Spearman correlation analyses (P < 0.05 indicates significant effect).
Analyze heterogeneity using chi-squared and I2 tests (P < 0.1 or I2 > 50% indicates significant heterogeneity).
Perform meta-regression analysis to explore sources of heterogeneity.
Test for publication bias using Deek’s funnel plot asymmetry test.
Apply two-sided statistical tests with a significance threshold of P < 0.05.
